co_mecca_area.blurb: Mecca is the largest sub-area of Nine Mile Bouldering, on Nine Mile Hill in Unaweep Canyon near Grand Junction, Colorado. It is pure bouldering, spread over dozens of named boulders and blocks. Grades run from V0 to V6, and most problems sit between V2 and V4. The rock on Nine Mile Hill is Burro sandstone. Mecca Boulder leans toward sloper-style problems and has an east face with good warm-ups; Moby Dick Boulder, Hueco Boulder and Birdhouse Boulder are other sizable stops. At the far western edge of the area the climbing is mostly vertical, with some slabs and slightly overhanging problems, and it feels set apart from the highway; the canyon wall brings shade in the later afternoon there. Across Unaweep Canyon, climbing is possible on almost any dry day.

id_massacre_rocks_state_park.blurb: Massacre Rocks State Park in east Idaho is the largest bouldering zone around Pocatello, and it is all boulders, with short walks between them. The rock is basalt: a handful of house-sized erratics plus many smaller blocks. Grades run from the easiest problems up to V8, with the bulk between V0 and V6, so moderates are plentiful and there is plenty for strong climbers too. Garden of the Gods is the biggest cluster, with the Bond Boulders, Parking Lot Boulders and Pinocchio next in size. Summer is too hot here, so fall and spring are the best seasons, and a sunny winter day can work as long as there is no snow on the ground.

sd_mohican_the.blurb: The Mohican is a cluster of walls in Spearfish Canyon, South Dakota, and the stone here is counted among the best in the canyon, whose rock quality improves the farther up it you go. The canyon is capped by bands of limestone, with pockets and technical movement common. Sport dominates, with a small group of boulders. Grades run mostly from 5.10 to 5.12, centered on 5.11 and 5.12, with a few 5.13s and some easier lines. The Asylum has the most routes and is notably technical, followed by Wars Wall, the Gully of Biblical Proportions and Red Light District. Canyon-wide, fall is the best season, dry and cooler, while summer is hot and humid; many crags face east or west and are best in the morning or evening.

wy_ok_corral.blurb: OK Corral is the largest sector of Wild Iris, a sport area on Limestone Mountain in the Lander area of Wyoming. Its walls are fairly short and face west, rising out of dense pine forest, so the crag stays shaded and cool. Nearly every route is sport, and it holds the most moderate climbing at Wild Iris, mostly in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, with grades running from the 5.4 range up to 5.13 and 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. The routes can feel a little sharp and are less polished than the best at other sectors, but they make a good day out, especially when shade matters. It splits into left, central and right sides. Across Wild Iris the rock is white, pocketed dolomite, and the season usually opens when the snow melts in early June and runs into late fall.

ca_conejo_mountain.blurb: Conejo Mountain, in the hills of Newbury Park on California's Central Coast, is mostly a bouldering venue with a smaller group of roped climbs. The rock is volcanic, and at Conejo Boulders it is breccia: brittle and sometimes sharp, so check topouts and flakes before trusting them. Boulder problems run mostly from V0 to V4 with a few harder ones, and roped grades span the 5.3 range to 5.12. Mystery Science Theater is the main roped wall; its climbs are brief and tiring, from steep to slabby, and many are reached from the ridge above and top-roped. Loose blocks are common, so wear a helmet. Spring and fall are the best seasons, with hot summers and cool winters, and the rock needs a day or two to dry after rain. Weekdays are quiet.

ca_eagle_creek_canyon.blurb: Eagle Creek Canyon is on the west side of Lake Tahoe, just west of Emerald Bay, with views over the lake. It is the West Shore's main hub for roped climbing. Trad leads, with a healthy amount of sport, some top-rope, and a little bouldering and alpine-style climbing. The rock is featured granite, and it gets very hot in direct sun on warm days; many of the cliffs can be climbed year-round when dry. Fourteen sub-areas are spread through the canyon. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, concentrated between 5.10 and 5.12. Mayhem Cove is a sport cluster, Eagle Lake Cliff and Eagle Lake Buttress are the major trad walls, and 90 Foot Wall is mostly top-rope and trad.
